title: Checkpoint: Plague and War
objective: After this level you can explain how famine, plague and gunpowder shook the medieval world.
summary: Famine, plague, revolt and cannon shook late medieval Europe and halved its population for a time, yet Europe proved resilient. A timeline from 1315 to 1485 ties the chapter together.

cards.headline: Chapter 9 finale: famine, plague, revolt, cannon. Was Europe falling apart?
cards.body: Put the whole chapter on one page, then decide: a dying age, or a tough one?

events.label: Rain ruins harvests: the Great Famine begins
The Statute of Labourers tries to freeze wages
Bosworth: Henry Tudor defeats Richard III

cards.headline: Old age, or a tough patch?
cards.body: Historians of the 15th and 16th centuries pictured the Middle Ages sinking into old age, and this chapter’s disasters seemed to prove it: the famine of 1315, the Black Death. Famine, plague, war and financial collapse cut Europe’s population, for a time, to about half of the 70 million people of 1300. Yet many historians now stress something else: resilience. Europe recovered in the late 14th and 15th centuries. A patient that sick shouldn’t have got up again. It did.

cards.headline: Chapter 9 complete
learned: Why famine, plague and war battered late medieval Europe, and how it proved resilient anyway.
Where the Black Death came from, how ships carried it west, and why how it spread is still debated.
How the plague made workers scarce, and why frozen wages and a poll tax led to the Peasants' Revolt.
Why cannon ended the age of castles and broke Constantinople's walls, ending the Byzantine Empire.

questions.prompt: Plague and war: which of these came in the right order?

options.label: The Great Famine, the Black Death reaches Messina, the Peasants’ Revolt
The Black Death reaches Messina, the Great Famine, the Peasants’ Revolt
options.rationale: The famine began in 1315, before the plague.

options.label: The Peasants’ Revolt, the Great Famine, the Black Death reaches Messina
The Great Famine, the Peasants’ Revolt, the Black Death reaches Messina
options.rationale: The plague (1347) came before the revolt.

questions.prompt: After the famine and plague of the 14th century, why do many historians now stress Europe’s resilience?

options.label: Nobody died in the Black Death after all
Europe’s population never fell
options.rationale: It fell for a time to about half.

options.label: Europe recovered in the late 14th and 15th centuries
The Middle Ages ended in 1315
options.rationale: The crisis came within the Middle Ages.

questions.explanation: Famine and plague halved Europe’s population for a time, but Europe recovered in the late 14th and 15th centuries.

questions.prompt: Plague and war: Constantinople in 1453 and Italy’s castles in 1494 both fell to what?
questions.explanation: Urban’s cannon pounded Constantinople’s walls, and French guns reduced castle after castle in 1494.

questions.prompt: Plague and war: plague kills many workers, then wages rise, then what, before the revolt of 1381?

options.label: A new plague ends the labour shortage
options.rationale: A law, not a plague, came next.

options.label: A law tries to freeze wages at pre-plague levels

questions.explanation: The Statute of Labourers (1351) tried to freeze wages; resentment, plus the poll tax of 1380, led to the revolt.
